scenes.title: What is Photosynthesis?
scenes.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy from the sun into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis is a vital process that sustains life on Earth.
scenes.visual_prompt: A simple diagram of a plant with sunlight and water, surrounded by a green glow.

scenes.title: Light-Dependent Reactions
scenes.explanation: The light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the chloroplast and involve the absorption of light energy by pigments such as chlorophyll.
scenes.narration: This stage converts light energy into ATP and NADPH.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of chlorophyll molecules absorbing light energy.

scenes.title: Calvin Cycle
scenes.explanation: The Calvin cycle, also known as the light-independent reactions, occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast and uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO2 into glucose.
scenes.narration: This stage produces glucose from CO2.
scenes.visual_prompt: An animation of the Calvin cycle, with molecules moving and reacting.

scenes.title: Importance of Photosynthesis
scenes.explanation: Photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth, as it provides oxygen and organic compounds for living organisms.
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis supports the food chain and is crucial for human survival.
scenes.visual_prompt: An illustration of a plant providing oxygen to an animal.
